## What this is

The first presentation-independent semantic model of EDOPro's duel protocol.

    raw MSG_* packet -> protocol decoder -> DuelEvent + DuelState

`client/` builds against a C++20 compiler and **nothing else**: no Qt, no QML, no
Irrlicht, no `ocgcore`, no card database. It is designed to run alongside the legacy
path, not instead of it, but that integration does not exist yet in this branch —
`DuelClient::ClientAnalyze` is untouched, and **no file in `gframe/` was modified**. Today
the model is exercised independently, against recorded duel streams: a standalone CLI tool
(`client/tools/semantic_trace_main.cpp`) and 69 unit tests.

Research first: [`docs/architecture/semantic-model.md`](docs/architecture/semantic-model.md)
records what the legacy client actually stores, read from upstream `54ea755a`, with line
references. [`docs/adr/0002`](docs/adr/0002-semantic-event-model.md) records the decisions.

> **Update (post pre-merge review):** this branch went through a focused review/hardening
> pass after the section below was first written — see
> [**Pre-merge review and hardening**](#pre-merge-review-and-hardening) near the bottom for
> exactly what changed, what the review got right, and the one place I pushed back with
> evidence rather than complying. The wording above ("presentation-independent semantic
> model," "designed to run alongside") is itself a correction the review prompted — the
> original read, in isolation, as claiming a live integration that does not exist.

## Architecture chosen

| Layer | Header | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | `card_identity.h` | `CardInstanceId`, `CardCode` — two strong enums, never interchangeable |
| Location | `card_location.h` | `Zone`, `CardLocation`, overlay as a modifier not a zone |
| Card | `card_state.h` | `CardState`, `CardPosition` |
| State | `duel_state.h` | "What is true now" — zones, life, turn, phase, chain |
| Events | `duel_event.h` | "What just happened" — a `std::variant` of 25 closed types |
| Decoder | `protocol_decoder.h` | Bytes in, events out, state mutated |
| Trace | `semantic_trace.h` | Deterministic golden rendering + honest coverage |

`DuelState` enforces **client-state integrity only** — one instance in one slot, moves
empty their source, chain links contiguous, material indices dense. Never game rules;
`ocgcore` owns those. `check_invariants()` re-derives every one of them from scratch, and
a unit test deliberately corrupts a model to prove the check can fail.

**Decoding is transactional.** `ProtocolDecoder::decode()` runs a handler against a private
copy of the state and commits it back only when the packet is fully accepted — a refused
packet (`Malformed`, `Inconsistent`, or either non-decoded status) leaves the real
`DuelState` exactly as it was, proven via a new whole-value `DuelState::operator==`, not a
field-by-field spot check. This was **not** true when this section was first written; see
the hardening section below.

## Semantic state types

Life points, `turn`, `turn_player`, `Phase`, `ChainLink`, and per card: `CardInstanceId`,
`CardCode` (optional by construction), `CardLocation`, `CardPosition`, optional ATK/DEF,
material list and back-reference, and a `tracked` flag.

There is deliberately no `matrix4`, no texture, no opacity, no animation frame, no QML
object. Compare `gframe/client_card.h`, where 21 renderer fields sit in the same struct as
a card's attack value.

## Event representation

`std::variant` of 25 event types. The set is closed and small, so exhaustive handling is
worth compile-time checking, and nothing needs polymorphic ownership.

**Events carry facts, never animation instructions.** `CardMoved` says a card went from
`HAND[p0:2]` to `MZONE[p0:1]`; *how long to animate that* is a presentation decision
derived from the fact. Two consequences worth naming:

- `CardMoved` reports the **resolved** destination. Piles renumber on insertion
  (`ClientField::AddCard`), so a UI told the *requested* sequence would animate to the
  wrong slot.
- `LifePointsChanged` carries `from`, `to` **and** the stated `amount`. Life clamps at
  zero, so lethal damage states more than it removes. Both are true.

## CardInstanceId strategy

**The protocol provides no stable instance id.** This was verified, not assumed:

- `loc_info` (`gframe/core_utils.cpp:281`) is `controller, location, sequence, position` —
  a *coordinate*, not an identity.
- A passcode is shared by every copy of a card, and is **0** whenever the recipient may not
  see the card. `MSG_SHUFFLE_DECK` sets every deck card's code back to 0 outright.
- The legacy client identifies a card by the identity of its `ClientCard` **heap object**,
  moving the same pointer between `ClientField`'s zone vectors as `MSG_MOVE` arrives.

So `client/` allocates its own: `enum class CardInstanceId : uint32_t`, from 1, never
reused. It is the legacy pointer identity made explicit and serialisable.

`DuelState` reproduces `AddCard`/`RemoveCard` **including their quirks** — deck sequence 0
inserts at the front, hand/graveyard/banished ignore the requested sequence, the extra deck
splits face-up from face-down via `extra_p_count` — so the two models can later be compared
slot for slot rather than approximately.

**Stated limit:** after `MSG_SHUFFLE_DECK` an instance id no longer denotes the same
physical card. Upstream does not permute its deck vector because it is not told the
permutation; it merely forgets every code. Ours does the same. Nothing downstream may
assume more.

## Hidden information

`CardCode::None` is a first-class, permanent state, not a gap to fill in. The model
represents known, unknown, face-down-with-known-code, face-up-with-unknown-code, and
identity arriving or being withdrawn later (`CardIdentityRevealed` /
`CardIdentityConcealed`).

**Honest caveat, also in the docs:** a `.yrpX` is an *unfiltered* recording. What the model
guarantees is that it never manufactures identity the stream did not state — not that the
stream was redacted. In a live duel the server filters, and the same decoder then holds
strictly less.

## MSG_* types supported (27)

`MSG_START`, `MSG_WIN`, `MSG_SHUFFLE_DECK`, `MSG_SHUFFLE_HAND`, `MSG_NEW_TURN`,
`MSG_NEW_PHASE`, `MSG_MOVE`, `MSG_POS_CHANGE`, `MSG_SET`, `MSG_SUMMONING`, `MSG_SUMMONED`,
`MSG_SPSUMMONING`, `MSG_SPSUMMONED`, `MSG_CHAINING`, `MSG_CHAINED`, `MSG_CHAIN_SOLVING`,
`MSG_CHAIN_SOLVED`, `MSG_CHAIN_END`, `MSG_DRAW`, `MSG_DAMAGE`, `MSG_RECOVER`,
`MSG_LPUPDATE`, `MSG_PAY_LPCOST`, `MSG_ATTACK`, `MSG_BATTLE`, `MSG_DAMAGE_STEP_START`,
`MSG_DAMAGE_STEP_END`.

Every layout was read from the corresponding `case` in `duelclient.cpp` and then checked
against payload lengths recorded in the committed M1 structural traces. Three details that
are easy to get wrong, and are documented: `MSG_POS_CHANGE` is **not** `loc_info` (all
single bytes in both revisions); `MSG_DRAW`'s first code belongs to `deck.back()`; and
`MSG_MOVE` applies a code under different conditions per branch, so returning a card to the
extra deck with code 0 genuinely conceals it.

Both protocol revisions are handled. `ProtocolVariant{compat}` narrows `loc_info`, counts
and description ids, as `replay_mode.cpp:86` derives from `REPLAY_LUA64`.

## Packet coverage — reported honestly, not as one percentage

| | duel-chains-battle | duel-extended |
|---|---|---|
| total packets | 990 | 1133 |
| **decoded** | **138** | **245** |
| known but not implemented | 852 | 888 |
| unknown ids | **0** | **0** |
| malformed | **0** | **0** |
| inconsistent | **0** | **0** |
| distinct types decoded | 24 | 19 |

Unchanged by the hardening pass: neither fixture ever produced a `Malformed` or
`Inconsistent` packet, so the transactional fix (which only changes behaviour on those
paths) altered no observable output for real data — confirmed by re-running the golden
comparison, byte-for-byte identical.

The large unsupported counts are almost entirely `MSG_UPDATE_DATA` (799 / 649) and
`MSG_UPDATE_CARD` (30 / 124) — the query stream. That is a deliberate omission, not an
oversight: it is the single biggest remaining slice and it is where ATK/DEF and card types
come from. The remainder is `MSG_CONFIRM_*`, `MSG_BECOME_TARGET`, `MSG_CARD_HINT` and
`MSG_PLAYER_HINT`.

`UnknownMessage`, `UnsupportedMessage`, `Malformed` and `Inconsistent` are four different
statuses precisely so this table cannot lie. Unsupported messages do not masquerade as
malformed ones, and every refusal of the latter two kinds is listed individually in the
trace with its reason.

## Example semantic trace

Real output from `duel-chains-battle.yrpX`:

```
   13 TurnStarted player=p0 turn=1
   14 PhaseChanged DRAW
   21 CardIdentityRevealed instance=35 code=70828912
   21 CardsDrawn player=p0 cards=[35]
   46 PhaseChanged MAIN1
   59 ChainLinkAdded link=1 instance=38 code=504700054 from=HAND[p0:2] trigger=HAND[p0:2] desc=529216363823104
   60 CardMoved instance=38 HAND[p0:2] -> GRAVE[p0:0] reason=COST|DISCARD
   77 ChainLinkResolving link=1
   78 CardIdentityRevealed instance=15 code=504700054
   78 CardMoved instance=15 DECK[p0:14] -> HAND[p0:5] reason=EFFECT
   82 HandShuffled player=p0 cards=6
   85 DeckShuffled player=p0 cards=33
   86 ChainLinkResolved link=1
   87 ChainEnded links=1
  248 AttackDeclared attacker=91 target=direct
  257 PositionChanged instance=37 FACEDOWN -> FACEUP
  277 CardCreated instance=111 at=MZONE[p0:0] code=73915052
  279 SummonAnnounced kind=SPECIAL code=73915052 at=MZONE[p0:0]
  324 AttackDeclared attacker=91 target=114
  360 CombatStatsRevealed instance=91 atk=1000 def=600
  377 CardRemoved instance=114 from=MZONE[p0:3] reason=DESTROY|BATTLE
```

…followed by a coverage table, the final state (`lp: p0=5800 p1=8000`, `invariants: ok`)
and every zone's contents.

## Tests

**69 C++ test cases in 6 CTest suites** (no test framework — a small registry-and-macros
harness, because adding a dependency to a library defined by having none would be a poor
trade):

- `duel_state` (17) — zone bookkeeping and every legacy quirk, material attach/detach and
  reindexing, refused moves changing nothing, life clamping, chain ordering, plus a test
  that deliberately corrupts a model to prove `check_invariants()` can fail. Two of the 17 were added in a second hardening round (see item 6 below).
- `protocol_decoder` (25) — every message layout, all four refusal statuses, the count
  guard against an absurd length, the compat variant, and a check that the supported-id
  list and the dispatch switch cannot drift apart.
- `hidden_information` (8) — unknown by default, unknown stays unknown, identity arriving
  late, shuffling withdrawing it, code 0 not erasing what is known, and position/identity
  being independent.
- `semantic_trace` (7) — packet framing round-trip and rejection, determinism, coverage
  arithmetic, no environmental leakage.
- `transactional_decoding` (9, **added in the hardening pass**) — the all-or-nothing decode
  guarantee, end to end, using whole-state equality. See the hardening section below.
- `legacy_perspective` (3, **added in the hardening pass**) — the legacy player-perspective
  formula, test-only, prep work for the deferred equivalence check.

**16 Python test cases** over real data and tooling: 8 semantic-golden tests (unchanged) and
8 new tests for `tools/generate_protocol_constants.py`'s drift-detection logic
(`tests/test_generate_protocol_constants.py`, **added in the hardening pass**).

## What the tests prove — and what they do not

**Prove:** the decoder reads 2,123 real recorded packets with zero malformed, zero unknown
and zero inconsistent; the model it builds is self-consistent at the end of both duels; the
events and final state are byte-for-byte reproducible; a refused packet leaves `DuelState`
provably, structurally unchanged; and the unit tests cover the compat protocol path and the
overlay/material path, which no committed fixture exercises.

**Do not prove**, and this is the same boundary as
[replay-regression.md](docs/architecture/replay-regression.md):

- **Nothing here runs `ocgcore`.** The fixtures are frozen recordings, so a green run says
  nothing about whether a live duel would emit the same messages.
- **No equivalence with the legacy client is demonstrated.** `gframe/` is untouched, so
  the two models have never been compared. That claim is not made anywhere in this branch.
  The normalization rule such a check will need (legacy is screen-relative via
  `Game::LocalPlayer`, the model is protocol-absolute) is now documented and pinned by a
  tested, deliberately test-only reference implementation — see the hardening section.
- The goldens lock in what the decoder *does*, which is why the property assertions above
  exist alongside them.
- Two fixtures is a small corpus. No XYZ materials, no tag duel, no compat-era replay.

## Exact gframe files touched

**None.** `git diff --stat master..HEAD -- gframe/ ocgcore/ irrlicht/ premake5.lua travis/`
is empty. So is `-- ui/`.

Two upstream headers are *read* by the constants generator and recorded in
`docs/UPSTREAM.md`: `gframe/ocgapi_constants.h` and `gframe/common.h`. The generated
header lives under `client/`, so an upstream change to a constant surfaces as a CI drift
failure rather than a merge conflict.

The additive hook in `DuelClient::ClientAnalyze` was deliberately deferred — see below.

## What remains unsupported

- **`MSG_UPDATE_DATA` / `MSG_UPDATE_CARD`** — the query stream (`CoreUtils::QueryStream`).
  ~75% of packets, and the source of ATK/DEF, level, type, counters and equip links.
- **Counters, equips, targets** — `MSG_ADD_COUNTER`, `MSG_EQUIP`, `MSG_CARD_TARGET`,
  `MSG_BECOME_TARGET`.
- **Every prompt** — `MSG_SELECT_*`. These need a response channel, a larger design
  question than M2.
- **`MSG_TAG_SWAP`, `MSG_RELOAD_FIELD`** — wholesale field replacement.
- **Flip summons, `MSG_SWAP`, `MSG_REVERSE_DECK`, `MSG_SHUFFLE_EXTRA`** — small, but
  unexercised by any committed fixture, so implementing them would be untested guesswork.
- **`LOCATION_SKILL`** — maps to `Zone::Unknown`; placement there is refused rather than
  silently folded into another zone.

## Recommended next M2 slice

1. **The additive hook.** Feed each packet to the semantic model alongside
   `ClientAnalyze`, behind a flag. Requires wiring `client/` into upstream's premake build
   — small, but it touches `premake5.lua`, so it deserves its own change.
2. **Then equivalence.** With the hook in place, assert that `ClientField`'s zones and
   `DuelState`'s agree after every packet across the fixtures, normalizing player
   perspective per `client/tests/legacy_perspective.h` / ADR 0002 Decision 7. This is the
   roadmap item this PR explicitly does **not** deliver.
3. **Then `MSG_UPDATE_DATA` / `MSG_UPDATE_CARD`.** Biggest coverage win by far, and the
   point at which the model becomes rich enough for a duel field. `CoreUtils::Query` is a
   well-specified ~100 lines; the care needed is around `QUERY_IS_HIDDEN` /
   `QUERY_IS_PUBLIC` and not leaking what the client should not hold. Also the point at
   which `handle_pos_change`'s strict-previous-position invariant should be re-examined —
   see the hardening section.

## Validation performed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `client/` clean build, `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror` | gcc 15.2, Linux (WSL) — clean |
| 6 CTest suites / 69 cases | 100% passed |
| Semantic goldens | 8/8, verified to **fail** with a precise diff when a golden is perturbed |
| Semantic goldens reproduce byte-for-byte from a clean tree | yes, unchanged by the hardening pass |
| M1 structural replay tests | 15/15, goldens unchanged |
| Message-id drift check | 96 ids, up to date |
| Protocol-constant drift check | 151 values, up to date |
| Protocol-constant drift *detection* itself | 8/8 new tests, including a forced-failure case |
| No artwork / scripts / databases committed | confirmed |
| No `gframe/` churn | zero files, re-confirmed after the hardening pass |
| `docs/UPSTREAM.md` updated | yes (files read, none modified) |

**Not verified locally, stated plainly:** the Qt shell and the upstream baseline were not
rebuilt on this machine — no Qt and no vcpkg tree in this WSL environment, and both are
byte-identical to `master` on this branch. CI covers both on this PR.

---

## Pre-merge review and hardening

This branch went through a focused review/hardening pass before merge. Five concerns were
raised; each was verified against source (and, where applicable, against both real
fixtures) before anything was changed, per this project's own standard for that kind of
claim. Four were confirmed and fixed. **One was investigated and found not to hold** — I
did not implement the requested change, and explain why below rather than complying by
default.

**1. Transactional decoding — confirmed, and worse than described.** The claim that a
refused packet never leaves `DuelState` half-mutated was false for four handlers, not the
two originally named: `MSG_MOVE` (both the ordinary-move and leaving-play branches),
`MSG_POS_CHANGE` (found during this audit), and `MSG_BATTLE`. Each applies a mutation
(identity, position, or combat stats) before a later step in the same handler that can
still fail. Fixed centrally rather than handler by handler: `ProtocolDecoder::decode()` now
runs against a private copy of the state and commits it back only once the packet is fully
accepted. Verified with a new whole-value `DuelState::operator==` and 9 new tests
(`test_transactional_decoding.cpp`) exercising all four handlers plus the three
non-`Decoded` statuses. Full writeup: [ADR 0002, Decision 6](docs/adr/0002-semantic-event-model.md).

**2. MSG_POS_CHANGE strictness — investigated, not changed.** The concern: since
`MSG_UPDATE_DATA`/`MSG_UPDATE_CARD` are undecoded, and legacy `ClientCard::UpdateInfo` *does*
write position from a bare `QUERY_POSITION` independently of `MSG_POS_CHANGE`, the model's
strict previous-position check could misfire on a healthy stream. Investigated directly
rather than weakened on the strength of the argument alone. It does not hold for this
slice: every position this model can observe already arrives through `MSG_MOVE` (which
always carries a destination position) or through `MSG_POS_CHANGE` itself —
`QUERY_POSITION` mirrors state already announced via one of those two decoded channels,
not an independent source of drift. Corroborated empirically against both real fixtures:
773 and 799 `MSG_UPDATE_DATA`/`MSG_UPDATE_CARD` packets respectively, heavily interleaved
with real position changes, **zero** false-positive `Inconsistent` results in either. The
check is unchanged; a code comment at `handle_pos_change` and a note in
`semantic-model.md` §7 record the investigation and its forward-looking caveat — this
reasoning covers the current 27-message slice, and should be re-examined the moment
`MSG_UPDATE_DATA`/`MSG_UPDATE_CARD` are actually decoded.

**3. Player perspective — confirmed accurate, now pinned by a tested reference.**
`Game::LocalPlayer` (`gframe/game.cpp`) is exactly `dInfo.isFirst ? player : 1 - player`,
applied at every `duelclient.cpp` handler before touching `dInfo.lp[]`/`ClientField`'s zone
arrays, which do no remapping themselves. `client/` stays protocol-absolute, deliberately —
that claim in `semantic-model.md` §4 was already correct. What was missing: an explicit,
testable statement of the normalization a future equivalence checker must apply. Added
`client/tests/legacy_perspective.h` (a small, **test-only** reference implementation, kept
out of `edopro_next_client` itself so perspective cannot leak into the semantic model) and
`test_legacy_perspective.cpp` (3 tests: `isFirst` true, `isFirst` false, and the involution
property). No live hook was implemented, per the review's own instruction not to. Full
writeup: [ADR 0002, Decision 7](docs/adr/0002-semantic-event-model.md).

**4. Wording — confirmed for this PR body, not for the tracked docs.** An audit of
README.md, `semantic-model.md`, ADR 0002, and this PR body found the four tracked files
already carefully hedged (no changes needed beyond one opening-line tightening in ADR 0002
made for consistency), but this PR body's own "It runs alongside the legacy path" and "the
first ... representation of a live Yu-Gi-Oh duel" read, in isolation, as claiming an
already-live integration. Both are corrected at the top of this description.

**5. Constants-generator drift detection — confirmed and fixed.**
`tools/generate_protocol_constants.py --check` compared only the rendered header text
against the committed one; a relevant constant `collect()` could not evaluate (e.g. a
future `#define LOCATION_FOO (1 << 12)`) was silently dropped and never surfaced in
`--check`'s output, only in the plain-write path CI does not run. Fixed: `--check` now
fails and names every such constant. 8 new tests
(`tests/test_generate_protocol_constants.py`) exercise this against scratch copies of the
real upstream headers — `gframe/` itself is never touched, confirmed via `git status`
before and after every run — including a positive-control test proving the fix isn't
merely stricter than necessary.

**6. Material location staleness — found by a separate automated reviewer, confirmed and
fixed.** After the review above landed, an automated PR reviewer (chatgpt-codex-connector)
flagged that `place()` finalised a host card's own `location` on every call but never
refreshed the mirror copy each attached material keeps for `at()`'s O(1) lookup — a host
that repositioned, or changed controller, while still carrying material left every attached
material's `CardState::location` naming the host's *previous* slot, and
`check_invariants()` did not catch it (it checked `overlay_index` but not that the mirrored
controller/zone/sequence actually matched). Verified against source, fixed in `place()`, and
`check_invariants()` strengthened to check the mirrored fields directly so this class of
drift cannot silently regress. Two new tests
(`moving_a_host_carries_its_material_along`,
`invariant_check_notices_a_material_naming_a_stale_host_location`). Semantic goldens
unaffected — the trace renderer never printed a material's location field.

**Not done, deliberately, per explicit instruction:** `MSG_UPDATE_DATA`/`MSG_UPDATE_CARD`,
prompts, counters, equips, targets, the live `ClientAnalyze` hook, premake integration,
and legacy/model equivalence. This was a correctness/hardening pass on the existing 27
messages and tooling, not a scope expansion.
